summary: Resent with chart. Hold/accumulate slowly (6/10). Breakout to ₹4,045 high on ~6x volume, now retesting ₹3,740. Start 25% near ₹3,740; add at ₹3,000–3,150 and ₹2,650–2,750.
body_md:
# Acutaas Chemicals (ACUTAAS): 3-year investment view

As of 8 Nov 2026 (price is the 6 Nov close). Built mainly from management commentary on the Q3 FY26, Q4 FY26 and Q2 FY27 calls, plus the financials.

## 1. Verdict

| | |
|---|---|
| Call | **Hold / accumulate slowly. Not a full-size buy at today's price** |
| Conviction | 6/10 |
| Price, market cap | ₹3,787, ₹31,000 cr |
| Valuation | 70.6x trailing EPS, about 61x FY27E, 48x FY28E |
| Type | A real compounder that the market already prices as one |
| Better buy zone | ₹3,000–3,150 (about 38–40x FY28E and the floor of the Jul–Oct base); add more at ₹2,650–2,750 if a weak quarter brings it there |
| Chart | Strong but stretched: an all-time-high breakout on about 6x volume, now retesting ₹3,740 (section 8) |
| Bad-case value | About ₹1,600–1,900 if the CDMO ramp stalls and the multiple falls to the high 20s |

**Thesis.** This is now a high-margin CDMO business. It makes advanced intermediates for originator drugs (Fermion/Orion and others) and generics like apixaban and rivaroxaban. Management has beaten and raised its guidance three times in a row. The ₹1,000 cr CDMO target came a year early (FY27, not FY28), and they are targeting ₹2,000 cr by FY30 **with no extra capex needed**. Battery chemicals and Korean semiconductor chemicals add two more growth engines, paid for from internal cash. The company has no debt.

**Anti-thesis.** At 61x this year's earnings, the price already assumes about 30% profit growth every year for ten years (see the reverse DCF in section 7). Profit should compound about 25–30%, but the P/E will probably shrink as growth slows, and that eats most of the return. Management also won't disclose its CDMO mix or how concentrated it is in its top product. That is the single biggest unknown.

## 2. Identity

- "Acutas" here is **Acutaas Chemicals Ltd**, formerly **Ami Organics Ltd** (old NSE symbol AMIORG; BSE 543349; NSE ACUTAAS). It listed in Sept 2021 and is based in Surat, Gujarat.
- Promoters: Naresh Patel (Chairman and MD) and Chetan Vaghasia (Wholetime Director). VP Strategy Abhishek Patel and CFO Bhavin Shah take most questions on the calls.
- It is a main-board stock, not F&O. It is currently on NSE's **ASM list**, which means higher margins on trades.

## 3. Business today

| Segment (Q2 FY27) | Revenue | YoY | Share |
|---|---|---|---|
| Advanced pharma intermediates (incl. CDMO) | ₹402 cr | +53% | 92% |
| Speciality chemicals (parabens, BFC, now battery) | ₹35 cr | −20% | 8% |

- **CDMO.** It makes intermediates under long contracts with originators. Fermion (Orion, Finland) signed a 10-year supply deal in Nov 2022 and another multi-year deal in Sept 2023. Five CDMO products were commercial by Jan 2026. Four more were validated in FY26 and are ramping in FY27. Management says 8–9 products will start contributing over the next 12–18 months.
- **Generic intermediates.** These include apixaban and rivaroxaban. This part grows in high single digits, and management is deliberately dropping low-margin products.
- **Speciality.** The parabens are commodity-like and being phased out. Baba Fine Chemicals (BFC), a subsidiary, makes electronic chemicals. Its shipments paused after its US customer changed owners; they have since resumed.
- **Export-led.** Exports were about 74% of FY25 sales, to more than 55 countries, with very little direct US exposure (CARE, Dec 2025). Shipments go out CIF, so the customer handles US customs (Q3 FY26 call).
- **Plants.** Sachin (USFDA EIR twice, PMDA approved), Ankleshwar (PMDA; only 30–40% used, so room to grow), Jhagadia (battery chemicals) and a new Korea plant (semiconductor chemicals).

Revenue quality: **High for CDMO, which runs on contracts with originators and is sticky. Medium overall**, because one or two products probably carry the CDMO book and nothing is disclosed about them.

## 4. Financials

₹ crore, consolidated (Screener; CARE).

| | FY22 | FY23 | FY24 | FY25 | FY26 | TTM |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Sales | 520 | 617 | 717 | 1,007 | 1,339 | 1,593 |
| EBITDA | 105 | 123 | 128 | 232 | 480 | 623 |
| EBITDA margin | 20% | 20% | 18% | 23% | 36% | 39% |
| Net profit | 72 | 83 | 49 | 160 | 356 | 439 |
| EPS (₹) | 9.9 | 11.4 | 5.8 | 19.4 | 43.5 | 53.6 |
| ROCE | 24% | 21% | 16% | 20% | 32% | 32% |

| Quarter | Q3 FY26 | Q4 FY26 | Q1 FY27 | Q2 FY27 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Sales | 393 | 433 | 330 | 437 |
| EBITDA margin | 38% | 42% | 34% | 40% |
| PAT | 106 | 134 | 75 | 123 |

What stands out:

- **Margins have doubled** from 18% (FY24) to 40% (Q2 FY27). Gross margin is 62%. Management says this comes from product mix: CDMO share went up while raw-material costs did not fall (Q2 FY27 call). That makes the margin structural rather than luck, but only as long as the CDMO mix holds.
- **Profit is real cash.** Operating cash flow was 95% of profit over FY24–FY26 (₹535 cr against ₹565 cr).
- **Free cash flow has been negative every year from FY23 to FY26** (₹−298 cr in total). That reflects heavy capex for Ankleshwar, Jhagadia and Korea. Capex is now slowing (₹300 cr in FY27, about ₹200 cr a year after that per PL), so FCF should turn clearly positive from FY27–FY28.
- **Working capital is the weak spot.** The cash cycle went from 107 days (FY22) to 149 (FY26). Working-capital days rose from 99 to 115 between Q1 and Q2 FY27. Management's target is about 100 days.
- **The balance sheet is very strong.** Borrowings are ₹15 cr and net cash about ₹300 cr (Sept 2026). Interest is covered more than 100x. CARE rates it A+/Stable.

## 5. What management has said (the commentary)

### Guidance track record: it keeps beating

| When | Promise | Outcome |
|---|---|---|
| Start of FY26 | ~25% revenue growth | Raised to ~30% in Jan 2026; delivered +33% |
| Start of FY26 | 28–30% EBITDA margin | Raised to 32–35%; delivered ~36% |
| Q4 FY26 (May 2026) | "Confident of delivering 25% revenue growth in FY27" | Raised to ~30% in Oct 2026 after H1 grew +49% |
| Jan 2026 | CDMO above ₹1,000 cr by FY28 | Now expected in FY27, a year early |
| Q2 FY27 | 38–40% EBITDA margin from FY27 | H1 at 37.7%, Q2 at 40.3% |
| FY26 | Battery chemicals commercial by Q4 FY26 | Slipped about one quarter; first revenue came in Q2 FY27 |
| FY26 | Pilot plant and battery phase-2 capex | Delayed by late equipment |

**Concall credibility: 8/10.** Management sets guidance it can beat on the core business. The new projects have slipped by a quarter or two.

### Key claims from the Q2 FY27 call (27 Oct 2026)

- FY27 revenue growth raised from 25% to **~30%**. EBITDA margin guided at **38–40%**.
- CDMO: **₹1,000 cr in FY27, ₹2,000 cr by FY30.** The second ₹1,000 cr is to be "more diversified across molecules and customers". **No new capex is needed** to reach ₹2,000 cr. Planning for the next expansion has started with land acquisition.
- Ankleshwar Unit 2 (about ₹330 cr invested) was 30% used in Q2. Management expects about 40% by the end of FY27 and peak use in FY28. That is cheap growth, because the asset is already paid for.
- Capex of ₹124 cr in H1 FY27 and about ₹300 cr for the full year: about ₹100 cr for an electronic-grade chemicals plant, ₹45 cr for battery phase 2, and the rest maintenance.

### Tone

The tone is confident but guarded. Answers on numbers are transparent. On mix they are evasive: *"I'm afraid I will not be able to give you this specific number"* (on CDMO share of revenue) and *"I will not able to give you any guidance on the product mix in next 3 years' time"* (Q3 FY26 call). Analysts pushed hard on product concentration and BFC guidance, and both were declined.

## 6. Future scope: the three growth engines

Naresh Patel's stated aim is for pharma, battery and semiconductor chemicals to each become "independent self-sustaining growth engines" by FY28.

**1. Pharma CDMO (the main engine, about 85–90% of value).**
- The CDMO business is set to double from ₹1,000 cr to ₹2,000 cr between FY27 and FY30, roughly 26% a year, using capacity that already exists.
- Each new validated CDMO product has ₹50–100 cr of peak revenue potential (Q4 FY26 call).
- The company has developed more than 680 molecules, and a new R&D centre with about 10x the current capacity is planned.

**2. Battery chemicals (electrolyte additives VC and FEC).**
- The Jhagadia block opened on 19 Jan 2026 and **first commercial revenue came in Q2 FY27**.
- The third product has started shipping and validation batches of the fourth have been sent to customers.
- Customers are battery-cell OEMs on long-term contracts. Pricing is linked to raw materials and the rupee, at early double-digit dollars per kg.
- Investment so far is about ₹220 cr, plus ₹45 cr for phase 2 in H2 FY27.
- On margins, management said they "will be below the traditional Pharma Intermediates business and above the existing paraben". That points to roughly 20–30% EBITDA.
- Analyst view: this is a real option on India's and the world's EV and storage build-out. Chinese suppliers dominate VC and FEC, and price swings there are the main risk. Expect only a modest contribution until FY28.

**3. Semiconductor and electronic chemicals.**
- **Indichem Korea** is a 75:25 JV with J&Materials, with about ₹200 cr invested. The plant opened ahead of schedule in Q2 FY27. Qualification batches have gone to Korean customers. FY28 is the ramp-up year, and it will make chemicals for photoresist, packaging and etching. Asset turnover is about 1x, with "high EBITDA margin".
- **Electronic-grade chemicals plant in India**: about ₹100 cr capex, production from H1 FY29, asset turnover of at least 3x.
- **BFC** is selling Heraeus-line products into new countries, with a Japanese customer "very promising".
- Analyst view: semiconductor chemicals are slow to qualify (18–36 months) but very sticky once approved. This is real upside for FY29–FY31, but none of it is proven yet.

**Where this could land.** Management guides about 30% growth for FY27 and 25%+ for the next few years. That would take revenue from ₹1,339 cr (FY26) to roughly ₹3,000–3,500 cr in FY30 and profit to roughly ₹800–950 cr. PL's estimates (27 Oct 2026) have FY29 sales of ₹2,966 cr and PAT of ₹799 cr.

## 7. Valuation

| Measure | Value |
|---|---|
| P/E on trailing EPS of ₹53.6 | 70.6x |
| P/E on FY27E EPS of ₹62 (PL) | 61x |
| P/E on FY28E EPS of ₹79.5 (PL) | 48x |
| P/E on FY29E EPS of ₹97.6 (PL) | 39x |
| Own 4–5 year median P/E (value screen) | about 61x |
| Healthcare sector median P/E | about 53x |
| Price to book | about 16.7x |

**Reverse DCF** (cost of equity 12.5%, terminal growth 5.5%): today's ₹31,000 cr price needs **about 32% profit CAGR for 10 years** from TTM profit of ₹439 cr. A pure DCF at a more realistic 22–25% growth gives roughly ₹1,900–2,350. In other words, the price assumes everything goes right.

**Where the stock could be in 3 years** (Nov 2029, valued on FY30 EPS; my own model):

| Case | FY30 revenue | FY30 PAT | Exit P/E | Price | 3-yr return a year |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Bull: guidance beaten, battery and semis kick in | ₹3,660 cr | ₹1,044 cr | 50x | ~₹6,400 | ~19% |
| Management path: ~38/26/25/22% growth, 27% PAT margin | ₹3,550 cr | ₹959 cr | 40–45x | ₹4,700–5,300 | 7–12% |
| Base: 33/24/20/18% growth | ₹3,130 cr | ₹813 cr | 40x | ~₹4,000 | ~2% |
| Bear: CDMO product falls off, China undercuts battery | ₹2,270 cr | ₹476 cr | 28x | ~₹1,600 | about −25% |

The key point: profit can grow about 2.5x in four years and the stock can still return only single digits from here, because the P/E falls from 60s to the 40s. The return depends far more on **the price you pay** than on whether the business delivers.

**Stress test on FY28** (base revenue ₹2,210 cr, 40% of costs fixed):

| Revenue | FY28 EPS | Value at 30x |
|---|---|---|
| Base | ₹71 | ₹2,140 |
| −10% | ₹59 | ₹1,760 |
| −20% | ₹46 | ₹1,390 |
| −30% | ₹34 | ₹1,010 |

A 500 bp margin cut gives FY28 EPS of ₹61, worth ₹1,840 at 30x.

## 8. Chart analysis

![ACUTAAS weekly and daily chart](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Parth1501/nse-swing-data/434b5f0/data/charts/2026-11-08/ACUTAAS_long.png)

This reading uses price and volume only, from weekly candles over about 3 years and daily candles over 6 months. The data runs to 8 Nov, including the Diwali Muhurat session at ₹3,927 on very thin volume.

**Price verdict: Strong but stretched.** The trend agrees with the fundamentals. The price itself is already far from good support.

**Trend structure.** The stock has made higher highs and higher lows since the January 2026 low of ₹1,570 (week of 23 Jan). It is up about 2.6x in ten months, up 114% in a year, and at an all-time high. Stage: **markup**. There has been no lower low on the weekly chart all year.

**Base, July to October 2026.** After the July high of ₹3,740 (week of 10 Jul), the stock moved sideways for about 15 weeks between **₹3,025 and ₹3,740**. The lows came in the weeks of 7 Aug (₹3,025) and 9 Oct (₹3,031). There was one lower high, at ₹3,510 in the week of 25 Sept. Volume was quiet through the base. That pattern looks like holders sitting tight, not distribution.

**Breakout, week of 30 Oct.** After the Q2 results (27 Oct) the stock jumped **+27.6% in one week**, from ₹3,138 to ₹4,004. Volume that week was 1.23 crore shares, **about 5.9x the 52-week average**. A move that size on that volume usually means large buyers stepping in, which fits the FII stake rising from 16.9% to 22.6%.

**Pullback, week of 6 Nov.** The stock touched the **₹4,045 all-time high** on 2 Nov, then slipped to ₹3,705 and closed at ₹3,787. That puts it right on the old ₹3,740 top, which should now act as support. Volume fell back to normal (about 0.95x average). A dip on light volume back to the breakout level is the healthy way for a breakout to behave.

| Level | What it is | Distance from ₹3,787 |
|---|---|---|
| ₹4,045 | All-time high, the only level overhead | +7% |
| ₹3,740 | Old July top, now being retested as support | −1% |
| ₹3,510 | September lower high, inside the base | −7% |
| ₹3,025–3,031 | Floor of the base (Aug and Oct lows) | −20% |
| ₹2,635 | April 2026 high, the earlier breakout level | −30% |

**What the chart says for a 3-year buyer.**

- **Holding ₹3,700–3,750 on weekly closes** confirms the breakout. A small first buy here is reasonable (tranche 1 in section 11).
- **A weekly close below ₹3,510** would mean the breakout failed. The stock would probably drift back into the base towards ₹3,030–3,150. That is the **add zone 1** shown in green, and it matches about 38–40x FY28E earnings from section 7.
- **A weekly close below ₹3,000** would break the year-long pattern of higher lows. The next support is ₹2,635–2,750, the **add zone 2** in green. The stock would only get there on a bad quarter or a market-wide selloff. It is a level to review the thesis, not a stop-loss.
- **Above ₹4,045** there is no overhead supply, so the price can run, but buying an extended move at about 65x earnings leaves little room for error. Don't chase it; let a pullback or a base come to you.
- **ASM listing** (higher margin) and the jump in retail holders (1.09 lakh to 1.47 lakh in a year) usually mean bigger swings both ways.

## 9. Governance and ownership

- **Promoter holding is 32.66%, flat for six quarters, with no pledge.** It fell about 6% over three years through a preferential issue and stake sales. A lowish promoter stake is the main governance watch item.
- **FIIs went from 16.9% to 22.6% in five quarters**, so foreign funds are accumulating. DIIs went from 22.4% to 19.4%.
- **Shareholders went from 1.09 lakh to 1.47 lakh in a year**, so retail is crowding in.
- **No auditor, CFO or director exits.** The 2 Nov 2026 notice was only a new operations head (Dr Ashish Pandey) for Units 2 and 3, with two GMs now reporting to him.
- CARE A+/Stable, A1+ (Dec 2025). The board has eight members, four of them independent.
- **Subsidiaries are getting complex**: BFC, Acutaas Electrolytes, Acutaas Advance Materials, Enchem, Indichem Korea JV and Ami Onco-Theranostics JV. Watch related-party flows.

Scores: earnings quality 8/10 (cash backs the profit, but working capital is rising), capital allocation 7/10 (self-funded, incremental ROCE above 30%, a little dilution in FY25), governance 7/10, management credibility High.

## 10. Risks that would break the thesis

1. **CDMO concentration.** One originator molecule probably drives a large share of CDMO. If that drug's volumes fall, a second source takes share, or the customer destocks, growth could drop sharply. Management won't disclose the mix. *Early warning:* a QoQ fall in advanced-intermediates revenue that is not seasonal, or silence on new contracts.
2. **Margin peak.** 40% EBITDA is exceptional for an intermediates maker. Battery chemicals will dilute it, and price cuts from customers usually come once volumes scale. *Early warning:* gross margin below 57% for two quarters.
3. **China.** Chinese players dominate VC/FEC electrolyte additives and many pharma intermediates. *Early warning:* battery revenue stalling at the 3rd and 4th products.
4. **Execution on new projects.** The Korea JV and electronic-grade plant are new technologies. Past slippage has been one or two quarters.
5. **Working capital.** Days crept from 99 to 115 in a single quarter.
6. **Valuation and flows.** ASM listing, retail crowding and a 115% one-year rally mean a 25–35% drawdown on a weak quarter is very possible, even if the business is fine.

## 11. How to buy (3-year approach)

Analysis only, not advice. Fit it to your own risk.

1. **Start small now.** Put in about 25% of what you plan to own at ₹3,700–3,850, while the stock retests its ₹3,740 breakout level (section 8). The trend is strong, and you may never get the dip.
2. **Add on weakness.** Put the next 35% at **₹3,000–3,150**, where earlier weekly supports sit (₹3,120 and ₹3,031) and the price is 38–40x FY28E.
3. **Add the rest on a correction or proof.** Put the last 40% at **₹2,650–2,750** (weekly support ₹2,635) if a weak quarter brings it there. Otherwise add after Q4 FY27 results (around May 2027) if CDMO reaches ₹1,000 cr and battery revenue is visible.
4. **Spread it over 6–9 months** around results dates (late Jan, early May, late Jul, late Oct). The Q1 quarter is seasonally weak, so June–July often gives better prices.
5. **Size.** Keep it to 5–7% of a long-term portfolio, given the concentration and valuation risk.
6. **Exit or review triggers** (these are thesis checks, not price stops):
   - FY27 growth comes in below 22%, or FY28 guidance is below 20%
   - EBITDA margin falls below 34% for two quarters
   - Promoter stake falls or any pledge appears
   - Management cuts the ₹2,000 cr CDMO FY30 target

## 12. What to track each quarter

- CDMO revenue run-rate: ₹1,000 cr in FY27 means about ₹290 cr a quarter by Q4
- Advanced-intermediates growth, and whether management names the 4 new CDMO molecules
- Gross margin of 58% or more, and EBITDA margin of 38–40%
- Battery revenue from the 3rd and 4th products and the phase-2 start
- Korea JV qualification wins and first FY28 orders
- Working capital back towards 100 days
- FCF turning positive in FY27

**Bottom line: a genuine compounder at a full price. Profits will compound, but at 61x the buyer is paying for FY29 today. Buy slowly; the best returns come below ₹3,150.**
